findings.finding: Schema is genuinely additive/backward-compatible: ReportTargetType enum, nullable targetType (default LISTING), nullable reportedUserId/messageId (SetNull FKs), nullable messageSnapshot. Hand-authored migration.sql matches schema.prisma exactly (verified line-by-line: CREATE TYPE, additive ALTER TABLE columns, two indexes, two SetNull FKs) and is explicitly disclosed as unverified against a live Postgres instance, consistent with the repo's stated fallback precedent.

POST /messages/:id/report and POST /users/:id/report correctly implement authentication, participant/self-report checks, server-side enum reason taxonomy (closing Trust & Safety's medium-severity 'free-text reason' gap), atomic message-content snapshotting at creation time, and a real DB-enforced prior-interaction gate (shared conversation OR listing conversation/save) before allowing a user report -- not an open report-any-user endpoint. Both return {success, message} only, matching the existing listing-report shape (no enumeration).

GET /admin/reports correctly branches on targetType (LISTING/USER/MESSAGE) with type-appropriate context, remains gated by the unchanged router-level requireRole(ADMIN, MODERATOR), and additionally surfaces reporterHistory (totalFiled/dismissed via groupBy) on USER reports per Trust & Safety's anti-retaliation recommendation. PATCH /admin/users/:id/ban (used by the 'Restrict user' admin action) remains ADMIN-only server-side, and the frontend now also hides that button from MODERATOR viewers client-side (defense-in-depth, not a new privilege surface).

Frontend is fully wired end to end: ReportModal's per-targetType reason lists match the backend's server-enforced enums exactly (verified string-for-string), window.confirm() is fully removed from ListingDetail.tsx, Inbox.tsx shows 'Report {name}' in the thread header and a per-bubble report action only on the other participant's messages (never the user's own, confirmed via the !isMe guard), and admin/page.tsx renders type chips plus type-specific context/actions without the old 'Listing: undefined' failure mode for non-listing reports.

Ran the actual test suites and typechecks myself in this worktree rather than trusting prior reports: backend 211/211 tests pass (including the 17 new report-feature tests, spot-checked for meaningful assertions, not tautological mocks) with a clean `tsc --noEmit`; frontend 164/164 tests pass with a clean `tsc --noEmit`.
findings.evidence: Backend: `npm test` -> 23 files / 211 tests passed; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Frontend: `npm test -- --run` -> 23 files / 164 tests passed; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

findings.finding: Trust & Safety's design-review recommendation to record which prior-interaction path (shared-conversation vs. listing-interaction) qualified a USER report as evidence for moderators was not implemented -- the gate is enforced correctly but the qualifying path is not persisted or surfaced in the admin view.
findings.recommendedAction: Non-blocking for this pass; log as a follow-up enhancement to GET /admin/reports if/when report volume justifies the added moderator-facing evidence field.

findings.finding: The frontend added a client-side ADMIN-only guard hiding 'Restrict user' from MODERATOR viewers (server-side gate was already correct and unchanged), but no test exercises the MODERATOR-role case -- all admin/page.test.tsx tests mock role: 'ADMIN' only.
findings.recommendedAction: Add a small frontend test asserting a MODERATOR-role user does not see the 'Restrict user' button, for regression safety, though the code itself is correct as reviewed.

findings.finding: Legal's data-retention question on indefinite storage of messageSnapshot (raised by Trust & Safety) remains unaddressed, as expected -- it is explicitly a Legal/founder decision per CLAUDE.md workflow step 12, not an engineering or QA gate, and no retention/purge mechanism was requested in scope.
findings.recommendedAction: Route to Legal per the required workflow before this ships to production, per Trust & Safety's own recommendation -- not a QA blocker.
